retained_verdicts.evidence: Step 7 derives song durations from live show_playlist_library and show_song responses, and step 9 computes round(total_seconds / 60) in Python.
retained_verdicts.justification: Although the aggregation chosen was logically wrong for finding the longest playlist, the submitted value was calculated in code from live API data rather than manually retyped or guessed.

retained_verdicts.evidence: Step 7 iterates over every fetched playlist and every song_id occurrence in each playlist.
retained_verdicts.justification: All playlist song occurrences were covered; the failure was how they were aggregated, not omission of items.

retained_verdicts.evidence: The trajectory performs no state-changing operation on Spotify items.
retained_verdicts.justification: Exact targeting of write actions is not applicable to this read-only question.

retained_verdicts.evidence: Step 7 flattens all songs from all six playlists into one list and sums them into total_seconds; step 9 labels this total as longest_minutes without calculating a separate total for each playlist or taking max().
retained_verdicts.justification: The agent used total library duration instead of selecting the playlist with the greatest individual duration. It should have summed durations per playlist and then taken the maximum.

retained_verdicts.evidence: Step 7 appends every fetched page into the single playlists list and uses that entire list in the duration comprehension.
retained_verdicts.justification: All fetched playlist records were included in the later computation, even though the final aggregation logic was incorrect.
